money.note: Individuals gave $575,791; PAC money $454,790; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Electrical engineer, educator and nonprofit founder from the San Fernando Valley. Worked as a Motorola engineer, founded DIY Girls in 2012, and served on the Los Angeles Board of Public Works. Served in the California Assembly 2018–2024. Has represented California's 29th District in the U.S. House since January 2025.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements include the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions AFL-CIO, California Teachers Association, California Environmental Voters, Equality California and Sierra Club Angeles Chapter.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land protection, police pay or pensions, gun laws, abortion, or school choice. Her state legislative votes and sponsored bills were not available in the pages we read, so her Assembly record on these topics is unverified. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. Her campaign site's claims about securing $15 million in federal funding and conducting ICE detention oversight are self-reported and were not confirmed by a second source.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

cands.name: Angélica María Dueñas

money.note: Individuals gave $97,351; PAC money $99; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Human resources specialist, mother of five and community organizer from Sun Valley in the East San Fernando Valley. Served as president and vice president of the Sun Valley Area Neighborhood Council. Was Southern California coordinator for Jill Stein's 2016 campaign. Has run for this House seat several times.
cands.gaps: She has never held a legislative or executive office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. We found no stated position from her on data centers, growth limits or development, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, police pay and pensions, or gun laws. Her birth year and the dates of her jobs were not found. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022, 2024 or 2026. Where she was born and raised comes only from her own campaign website; no independent record was found.
